concept.name: Aroon down
concept.definition: The downside counterpart in Chande's Aroon system: a measure of how recently price made a new n-period low, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the low was set in the current period.
concept.intuition: It tracks the freshness of new lows; a market printing new lows today has Aroon-Down at 100, and sustained 70-100 readings mark strong downtrends.
concept.mechanics: Aroon-Down = 100 x (n - periods since the n-period low) / n, default 25. Crosses of Aroon-Down above Aroon-Up, moves above 50, and surges to 100 are the three stages of an emerging downtrend signal.
concept.failure_modes: Same time-not-magnitude limitation as Aroon-Up; both lines can sit low together in consolidations, giving no directional read at all.
concept.misconceptions: A high Aroon-Down is a description of recent lows, not an oversold buy signal.
concept.example: With n = 25 and the 25-day low set 10 days ago: Aroon-Down = (25-10)/25 x 100 = 60.
